questions.stem: Why are alloys harder than pure metals?

options.text: Alloys have stronger metallic bonds than pure metals
Different sized atoms in alloys disrupt the regular layers, preventing them from sliding easily
Alloys contain covalent bonds as well as metallic bonds
Alloys have more delocalised electrons than pure metals

questions.explanation: In alloys, atoms of different sizes are mixed into the metal structure. These different sized atoms disrupt the regular arrangement of layers, so the layers cannot slide over each other as easily as in a pure metal. This makes alloys harder and stronger than the pure metals they are made from.
